text:
nina: Follow-up from the RFC review: proposal to centralize API negotiation in a 'compat broker' service that emits migration hints and negotiates whether to route through a translator or direct runtime. Quick sanity-check?
omar: central broker sounds handy for telemetry consolidation. Concern: single point of routing failure.
lee: agree with Omar. Can we make broker stateless and cache decisions in the smart-router? then broker is just policy.
tia: how does this differ from the earlier sidecar approach? I liked sidecar for streaming parity.
nina: broker handles policy + header synthesis (X-RW-Client-Version, X-RW-Migrate-To, X-RW-Compat-Mode). Sidecars handle heavy lifting for streaming transforms; broker decides route and adds headers.
omar: ok, so path: client -> edge -> broker (policy) -> route to [edge-translator | runtime-sidecar | runtime].
lee: what's the fail-open behavior? If broker is down, prefer direct runtime (no translation) or fail closed?
nina: fail-open to runtime to avoid blocking clients, but emit broker.unreachable metric and trigger alert. Also add a short cached policy TTL in edge so routing survives broker outages.
tia: telemetry set: broker.decision, broker.latency_ms, translator.hit, translator.error_type, migration_hint_seen. Also record client.version and tenant.id.
omar: we need a migration_hint lifecycle: hint levels = info, warn, enforce. Info -> header only, warn -> header + warning response code 299, enforce -> translate or reject.
lee: do we actually use 299? it's nonstandard but works for warnings. Might prefer standard 2xx with warning header.
nina: good call. Keep 2xx but add X-RW-Migration-Warning. Reserve 4xx for incompatible rejects.
tia: billing question: if broker routes to translator that adds tokens, ensure billing uses pre-translation token count. Document that explicitly.
omar: also ensure translator emits translation.transform_id in logs for tracing. Useful for investigating regressions.
lee: caching impact: broker must normalize/annotate caching keys so that translated and native requests map correctly when safe. Add a cache-safe bit in header.
nina: proposed header example:

X-RW-Client-Version: 3.2.1
X-RW-Migrate-To: v5
X-RW-Compat-Mode: translate
X-RW-Cache-Normalize: true

omar: SDKs should expose a helper that reads X-RW-Migrate-To and shows a console.warn recommending upgrade. Also auto-attach X-RW-Compat-Mode when user opts into automatic translation.
tia: ops: runbook items: broker error budget alarm, translator latency spike alarm, immediate global rollback flag, and per-tenant kill switch. Add step-by-step for false-positive migration errors.
lee: testing: create synthetic corpus with corner-case fields (tool-calling, function args, streaming partial frames). Use diff-run to compare shim vs native. Run on every canary.
nina: rollout plan: 1) internal tenants only (dev+alpha), 2) opt-in customers via header or flag, 3) gradual auto-sample 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with parity checks. Each step has hold period.
omar: hold criteria: no translator.error_rate > 0.5%, median latency delta < 20ms, token-count variance < 0.5%.
tia: add a safety-net: if output-parity divergence > threshold then auto-disable translator for that tenant.
lee: curious about security: broker must not leak X-RW-Migrate-To to downstream partners or logs in a way that reveals private schema. Use PII-safe masking in telemetry.
nina: agreed. Telemetry scrub rules in RFC addendum.
omar: can we avoid global state by pushing decision logic into smart-router with a declarative policy downloaded from broker? then broker becomes a policy author.
nina: yes that's plan B. Start with central broker + router cache, migrate to fully declarative policy sync later.
tia: timeline: spike for broker perf + failure modes (this sprint), translator POC for unary + streaming (next sprint), canary in 2 weeks.
lee: add quick curl example for opt-in header:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "X-RW-Compat-Mode: translate" \n  -H "X-RW-Client-Version: 3.2.1" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

nina: I'll update the RFC with headers, metrics names, and rollout gates. Will post draft for review tomorrow.
